title: Building interior, often used to test lighting -- and this case decides its geometry and its material binding

criterion.says: Building interior, often used to test lighting.

acceptanceClass.because: The framing rule's own direction -- azimuth 35 degrees, elevation 20 degrees -- over one body. Nothing here is analytic and nothing claims to be: what is compared is which pixels the two sides cover and what colour each body wears, over the whole boundary rather than any one edge.

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render. We do not aim to be bit-identical with Cycles.

subjects.name: Sponza
subjects.notes: Attributes NORMAL, POSITION, TANGENT, TEXCOORD_0. World bounds [-15.3676, -1.0115, -9.4625] to [14.3993, 11.4355, 8.8434]. It carries no material at all, and the file's own images are NOT read by this case: the material below declares its own colours, so what is compared is where the geometry is and which body wears which row.

source.pinReason: the corpus-wide pin every manifest in this tree already cites

camera.derivation: The framing rule of src/gltf/Framing.h, quoted so the runner can refuse a mismatch rather than trust it. World bounds [-15.367568112732783, -1.0115400260729146, -9.462457480692592] to [14.399265332365871, 11.435466363467981, 8.84340862316435], so centre = [-0.484151390183456, 5.211963168697533, -0.3095244287641208] and radius = 18.547891222601656 m. yfov = 2*atan(12/50) from a 50 mm lens on a 24 mm sensor height at sensor_fit VERTICAL. distance = radius / sin(yfov/2) / 0.6 = 132.46244566811163, and the eye is centre + (cos20*cos35, sin20, cos20*sin35) * distance. clipStart is distance - radius and clipEnd is distance + radius.
camera.note: The glTF carries no camera, so the framing rule supplies one. Roll is 0 because the rule sets it: a roll chosen here and nowhere else would make this subject's placement a second determination competing with the rule.

light.note: A diffuse surface under the factory world; no punctual source is declared.

world.note: Configured by not being configured. It is the illumination here because the material is diffuse and something has to arrive for it to be seen.

material.note: DIFFUSE AND NOT EMISSION, because this file declares no material to key a colour by. One colour, and the illumination is the factory world -- the arrangement `Triangle` already runs green. The preparer pins a Diffuse BSDF rather than Principled, so no specular lobe enters at IOR 1.5.

default.note: The binary mask and the emitted colour in one render. One sample per pixel with the box filter at its RNA minimum makes Cycles evaluate the same predicate a centre-sampling rasteriser does, because the integer raster coordinate is the pixel centre and the sample never leaves +/-0.005 px of it. A still costs one frame, so the full 1280x720 is affordable here where an animated case has to buy its grid.

notes: A coverage case. Its subject's own shading -- textures, metallic-roughness, and any extension it declares -- is NOT what this decides; `board:1363` records why no case takes the shading arm yet. What it does decide is that the file reads, the geometry lands where the oracle puts it, and each material row reaches its own body.
